title: Reading Drill — Testing temporary path closures — Preparing a second trial
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Testing temporary path closures — Preparing a second trial
passages.body:
**A** In Foxhaven, work on walkers following an old path when repairs begin had already produced a small collection of site observations. The park planner used this material to plan a second trial. The first report contained several different figures, but for the second trial the group agreed to publish one main outcome: entries onto closed paths.

**B** The group kept paired notices at junctions for the new trial, which was planned to run for four weeks. Volunteers were shown a sample record before starting. They were also asked to describe anything unusual in a separate note, so later readers could tell the difference between an ordinary value and one taken during a disruption.

**C** The trial design stated that walking events should be recorded even when everything else appeared normal. If this information was missing, the team would leave the field blank rather than infer an answer. It would publish a provisional finding and label it clearly if too few readings were available for a reliable result.
